title: Why Nepal Is Being Handed a Climate Bill It Cannot Pay

story.core_message: Nepal faces severe climate impacts and a massive funding gap, despite contributing almost nothing to the problem.
story.takeaway: The countries least responsible for climate change are being left with the largest bills, and the promised help is not arriving.
story.hook: Nepal is paying for a crisis it did not create.
story.ending: The world promised one hundred billion a year by 2020. It delivered eighty-three.
story.cta: Which other country do you think is being asked to pay a bill it never ran up?

claims.claim_text: Nepal is globally ranked fourth in terms of vulnerability to climate change.

More than 80 percent of property loss due to disasters in Nepal is attributable to climate hazards, particularly water-related events such as floods, landslides and Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs).
Nepal experienced flash floods and landslides in August 2018 across the southern border, amounting to US$600 million in damages.
In Nepal, 95% of greenhouse gas emissions are from agriculture and forestry sectors, with 77% from the forestry sector alone.

At COP16 in Cancun (2010), developed countries committed to mobilizing jointly US$100 billion per year by 2020 to address the needs of developing countries, a goal extended through 2025 at COP21 in Paris (2015).

According to OECD figures, climate finance provided and mobilized by developed countries reached US$83.3 billion in 2020 and US$89.6 billion in 2021, meaning the US$100 billion-per-year-by-2020 target was missed.
